transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I’m here because... for almost two years now, I’ve been dealing with this situation at work. I'm a music director, and after a commission a while back, I've just been unable to shake the certainty that a few people in my ensemble are quietly trying to undermine my work. 

They do it through, you know, sudden schedule changes, weird seating choices, and just little comments they make in rehearsals. They’ll show me emails or notes that supposedly explain it all away, but... I know what they're actually doing. It's just been weighing on me, so that's why I decided to come in.
Do you think these people are trying to undermine you because of something you've done, or is it because of who you are?

I'm really not sure, to be honest. I've tried to figure that out, but... I don't think it's anything specific I've done to them. We always seemed to get along fine before that commission. 

So I don't know if it's about who I am, or maybe they just resent my position as the director? I just haven't been able to pin down an exact reason for it. I just know what I'm seeing them do, even if I don't fully understand the why behind it.
Do you think these people are actually talking about undermining you when you're not around?

I don't really know if they're actually sitting around talking about it behind my back. I mean, I haven't overheard anything like that, or... or found any proof of them plotting together when I'm not in the room. It's more just... what I see happening right in front of me during rehearsals and the administrative stuff. So, I can't say for sure if they're having secret conversations about it.
Have you ever considered the possibility that you might be misinterpreting the actions of your ensemble members?

I mean, I've tried to look at it that way. I really have. But... no, I don't think I'm misinterpreting it. Like I said when we first sat down, for almost two years now, I've just had this absolute certainty about it. Ever since that commission, these few people in the ensemble... they just keep using these sudden schedule changes, weird seating arrangements, and those little pointed comments during rehearsal to quietly undermine what I'm doing. 

And, you know, they'll show me an email or some notes that supposedly explain why a schedule got moved or why someone is sitting somewhere else... but it doesn't change what I know they're actually doing. So, no, I don't think I'm misunderstanding them. I just know what's happening.
Have you felt like people are undermining you in any other parts of your life, outside of work?

No, not at all. It's really just... just that specific group at work. Outside of this whole issue with the ensemble, everything else is pretty normal. I still meet all my deadlines, I keep up with my composing... I even go for a run most mornings. And things at home with my wife are basically steady. So, no, I don't feel like anyone else is doing this. It's just confined to that one part of my job.
If someone were to provide you with very strong evidence that the ensemble members are not trying to undermine you, would you be able to change your mind about what's going on?

Honestly, I don't think so. Like I was just saying, they already try to show me things—emails or notes that supposedly explain why a schedule was changed or why the seating choices were altered. But it doesn't change my mind. For almost two years now, ever since that commission, I’ve just been completely unable to shake the certainty that a few people in the ensemble are using those exact things, along with their little comments in rehearsals, to quietly undermine my work. So, even if someone brought me what they considered really strong evidence, I... I just know what I see happening.
Do you think it's possible that your certainty about being undermined could be a product of your own mind rather than based on real actions by others?

I... no, I really don't think it's just in my head. I know we keep circling back to this, but like I said, I've had this absolute certainty for almost two years now. Ever since that commission, I just know that a few people in the ensemble are quietly trying to undermine my work. They use the schedule changes, the seating choices, the little comments during rehearsals. And I know they have their emails and their notes that supposedly explain it all away, but... I just know what's actually happening. It's real, not something my mind is making up.
Have you experienced any major life changes or stressful events outside of your work as a music director in the past two years?

No, not really. Like I mentioned before, things at home with my wife are pretty steady. There haven't been any big moves, no major health issues, or financial crises or anything like that. It's just been my normal routine—composing, running, dealing with the ensemble. The only real stress has been... well, what we've been talking about, with those few people at work. Outside of that, everything else has been completely ordinary.
Have you experienced the loss of a close friend or family member in the past two years?

No, I haven't. Like I said, everything outside of work has been pretty steady. Everyone in my family is doing fine, and I haven't lost any friends or anything like that. It's really just the situation with the ensemble that's been going on.
Do you feel like you have a strong support system outside of your work with the ensemble?

Yeah, I do. My wife is a huge support, obviously. We talk about most things, though I try not to bring up the ensemble stuff too much because it just stresses both of us out. And I have a couple of close friends from grad school that I still see pretty regularly. We'll grab a drink or go for a run. So yeah, I'd say I have a good support system. It's just... they don't really understand what's happening at work, because they aren't there to see it. But they're good people to have around.
Would anything be able to convince you that your ensemble members are not trying to undermine you?

I honestly don't think so. I mean, that's really why I'm here. For almost two years now, I've been completely unable to shake the certainty that this is happening. 

Right after that commission I mentioned, a few people in the ensemble started using schedule changes, seating choices, and just these little comments in rehearsals to quietly undermine my work. And they try to explain it away. They'll actually show me emails or rehearsal notes that supposedly explain why a schedule was changed or why someone was moved around, like it's just some innocent logistical thing. But even when they show me that stuff... it doesn't change anything. I just know what they're doing, and I can't shake it.
Have you ever felt like your thoughts or perceptions are not your own or are being influenced by something outside of yourself?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that. My thoughts are my own. I don't feel like anyone or anything is putting thoughts into my head or controlling how I see things. I just see what's happening at work, but it's definitely my own perception.
Have you noticed any changes in your behavior or how you're functioning as a music director since you started feeling like you're being undermined?

Well, the main thing is just that everything takes a lot more energy now. Rehearsals, even just sending professional emails... I find myself rereading every decision I make, and sometimes I have to ask for extra clarification from people just to make sure I'm not missing something they're trying to pull. But I'm still doing my job. I haven't lost any work over it, and I'm still taking care of myself and my home life. It's just more exhausting to get through the workday.
Have you ever heard voices or sounds that other people cannot hear?

No, I've never had anything like that happen. I don't hear voices or any sounds that aren't actually there. Everything I'm dealing with is just... it's just regular conversations and things people are actually saying and doing in real life.
Have you ever felt like someone else was out to get you before this situation with the ensemble began?

No, I haven't. Before this whole thing with the ensemble started, I never really had any issues like this. I've always had pretty normal, good working relationships with other musicians and directors. It's really just this current situation where things have felt... off. So, no, I've never felt targeted by anyone before this.
